**Cases I had to handle**, each with a test in `csv.test.ts`:
- **`\r` at the end of a chunk:** the stream waits for the next character. If it's `\n`, that's a row end. Otherwise, in a field that isn't quoted the `\r` belongs to the field; after a closing quote it's a SyntaxError, and so is a `\r` after a closing quote at the very end of the input.
- **`"` at the end of a chunk inside a quoted field:** the next character decides whether it's a doubled quote or the closing quote. A quoted field still open at `end()` throws.
- **Rows come out only once their whole row end has arrived**, so `"a\r"` gives nothing until the `\n` comes.
- **End of input:** a row end just before the end doesn't start an extra row. An empty input, or one holding only the byte-order mark (BOM), has no rows. A trailing `,` still produces a last row.
- **The BOM is dropped only at the very start of the input**, even if empty chunks come before it. Later in the input it is kept as text.
- **Error messages and offsets** match `parseCsv`'s, counted from the start of the whole input.

**Behaviour you didn't ask for:**
- After a SyntaxError, later `push` and `end` calls throw the same error again, so you can't silently get wrong rows.
- `push` or `end` after `end` throws a plain `Error`.

Delete either if you'd rather not have it.

**Tests:**
- Every 2-way split and the 1-character split of a set of tricky inputs.
- 20,000 random inputs (from `a b , " \r \n` and the BOM) cut into random chunks of 0–3 characters, compared with `parseCsv`, invalid inputs included.
- A timing test: 400k tiny chunks inside one quoted field must take no more than 40× as long as 10k chunks, plus 200 ms. This guards against work that grows with earlier input, but because it measures time it could be flaky on a heavily loaded machine.

I implemented `applyEdit` in `edit.ts` following its doc comment, and `bun test` passes (13 tests, 0 failures).

**How it works:**
- **Checks first:** an empty `old_text` returns an error telling you to "use write". If `old_text` and `new_text` are identical, the error says they are the "same".
- **Exact match:** if `old_text` appears once, it's replaced and the result gives the lines it covered. If it appears more than once without `replace_all`, the error says "matches N places" and gives the line of the first one. With `replace_all`, every occurrence is replaced; `from` is the first match's line and `to` is the last match's.
- **Whole lines, ignoring trailing whitespace:** one trailing newline on `old_text` or `new_text` is ignored. The matching lines are replaced by `new_text` as given. An empty `new_text` deletes the lines.
- **Whole lines, ignoring indentation:** same as above, but `new_text` is re-indented. On each non-blank line of `new_text`, `old_text`'s indentation is swapped for the file's (so spaces become tabs if the file uses tabs). Blank lines are left as they are.
- **More than one match** in either whole-line step is an error: "matches N places (lines 1, 3)". It doesn't fall through to the next step, because the looser match would find at least as many places.
- **No match:** the error says "not found". If the first non-blank line of `old_text`, trimmed, appears in the file, it adds "first line appears at line L1, L2", listing at most 5 lines.

**Choices the doc comment didn't settle:**
- When `replace_all` is set but there's no exact match, the two whole-line steps still run, and they need exactly one match.
- A line of `new_text` that doesn't start with `old_text`'s indentation is left as it is.
- Windows-style line endings (`\r\n`) aren't handled specially.

There's no git repository here, so I couldn't produce a diff to review. The only file changed is `edit.ts`, and only the function body.

I implemented `readSse` in `sse.ts`, and `bun test` passes: 8 tests, 0 failures.

How it works:
- **Chunks of any size:** incoming bytes go through a streaming `TextDecoder`, so a UTF-8 character split across chunks decodes correctly. Text is kept in a buffer, and each complete line is handled as soon as its `\n` arrives.
- **Line endings:** a trailing `\r` is removed from each line, so `\r\n` works even when the `\r` and `\n` arrive in different chunks.
- **Field rules:** lines starting with `:` are skipped. A line with no colon is a field with an empty value, and only the first space after the colon is dropped. `event` names the message, each `data` line is added and the lines are joined with `\n`, and all other fields are ignored.
- **Blank line:** this yields the message straight away if it had at least one `data` line, then clears both the event and the data. A message with an event but no data is dropped. When there is no event, the yielded object has only `data`, with no `event` key.
- **End of body:** the decoder is flushed and any last line without a newline is handled. Pending data is then yielded as one final message.
- **Cleanup:** the stream's reader lock is released in a `finally` block, so it is also freed if the caller stops reading early. This only releases the lock; it doesn't cancel the stream.

**What changed in `window.ts`:** the doc comment, the argument checks and the error messages are unchanged. The old version compared every event with every other event. The new one sorts event indices by time, then moves a sliding window across them while keeping a count of each key in a `Map`. Each event gets the window's distinct-key count, and results come back in the original order.

Choices made to keep the results identical:
- **Equal or earlier times later in the list:** all events at time ≤ `t` are added before the count is read, so later entries with the same or an earlier time are counted, as the doc comment says.
- **Window boundary:** the window's lower edge uses the old expression, `other.t > t - windowMs`, computed the same floating-point way. For example, with `t = 0.3` and `windowMs = 0.1`, an event at `0.2` is still inside.
- **Tiny windows:** when `windowMs` is so small next to `t` that `t - windowMs` rounds back to `t`, the old code returned 0, not even counting the event itself. The new code must do the same. A first draft could run past the end of the list in this case; I added a `lo < hi` guard to stop that.
- **Key comparison:** keys are compared with the same `Set`/`Map` semantics as before.

**Tests:** my changes to `window.test.ts` were blocked because it's an existing test file, so it is unchanged. The new tests are in `window.contract.test.ts` and cover:
- unordered input and equal times
- an excluded `t - windowMs` boundary and an included `t`
- the floating-point boundary and the tiny-window case
- exact key matching
- `RangeError` for a negative, NaN or infinite `windowMs`
- `TypeError` naming the first bad index
- a randomised comparison against the old algorithm
- the 200,000-event timing check

The timing test uses a real clock, so it could fail on a very slow CI machine.

There's no git repository here, so I couldn't review the change with `git diff`. I checked the final file contents directly instead.
